title: The Twofold Senses and the Phoenix
english: Who, hearing something or about someone, sees and hears with his own eye and ear? In answer to these things, it is not said wickedly, but that there is a twofold genus of sensations in us, mortal and immortal; and specifically for us rational beings, the immortal part is found to be intelligible. For the mortal is not our own essence, but is common and belongs to the irrational animals. The Scripture does not mean the sensations of the whole man, but says 'my eye and my ear see and hear' as in the things set forth.

Since the phoenix bears much fruit, and the cedar in Lebanon is very fruitful and many-rooted (Ps 92:12), it is fitting that the righteous man was compared to such much-fruitful things in the virtues according to their kinds and the various doctrines of the truth. For according to these things his blossom is compared to the phoenix, but also because of the firm and strong nature regarding the good, he is likened to the cedar in Lebanon; for the cedar is indeed dense and very thick, and the phoenix is ever-living and possessing a heart upward-stretching, to which the one who has treasured in heaven and therefore has his heart there is fittingly made similar. And since in the Song of Songs the bridegroom (and he is not the God Word) is said to be a phoenix, upon whom it is promised that he shall ascend and hold his heights, the bride (the perfect soul and the church) saying, 'I will ascend in the phoenix and hold his heights,' see, in this way the righteous man will blossom similarly, receiving from it the power to save the blossoming fruit. For those called female palms by the farmers receive from the male palm the occasion for preserving the fruit. Such is that upon whom the bride says she will ascend.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Palm and the Rivers of Truth
english: Those who interpret his palm as being divine teachings receive it as a fertile and protective thing for the fruits. And the bride who says these things, not being like the flowering of the righteous according to the palm, says, 'I will be made like the palm.' From this palm, one takes ornaments made from the branches of palms when celebrating the feast of the Tabernacles, and the victors carry from this the symbols of victory.

Those who imitate [the rivers] lift up the river that gladdens the city of God (Ps 92:3–4b), first by raising their mind, if they use the voices that interpret the things understood by them, so that from the waters of these many rivers they may become wonderful and worthy of acceptance through repentance and the taking up of virtue, whereas formerly, through arrogance, wealth, self-will, and vainglory, they were tossed about like the waves of the sea of human life. And it is possible also for these words of the divinely inspired writings of both the New and Old Testaments to be rivers, because they are drinkable and life-giving and cause fruitfulness. Indeed, the rivers lift up and toss about those who drink from them through the contemplation of the truth, making the tossings of the sea wonderful, as they are ready to be awakened, lifting up their voices from the voices of the rivers by thinking things in a God-befitting and sublime way. Regarding the tossings of the sea, according to the present thought, the so-called temptations also will be wonderful causes of salvation, appearing from the voices of the many drinkable waters; for it is indeed possible to see upon...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Victory in Trials and the Holiness of the Temple
english: Showing some to be victors over these trials and struggles. For blessed is the man who endures trial (Ps 92:4c), and the following. Stop if many things, from which the swellings of the sea become marvelous because of the voices, happen to the sea; for from its own things and from the men in them, the swellings of it become marvelous, being logically and prudently examined and known.

In the high and exalted words, the Lord is marvelous (Ps 92:5a), so that his testimonies, which are kindred to the spoken rights and laws, and he himself, God, are to be believed as high in which he is marvelous. It is possible to say that men are raised to divine things through faith and the rest of virtue, and even the angels and archangels in heaven are high, in whom the Lord is marvelous, having testimonies and sayings established and examined because he has spoken them with certain stability (Ps 92:5bc).

All those who have approached God become his dwelling-place, and it is truly fitting to be holy for the saints, not for one or two days, but for a length of days; thus the Initiator, desiring the dwelling-place of God to be a sanctification for a length of days, says: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys the temple of God, God destroys this one; for the temple of God is holy, and you indeed are [it]. For holiness and sanctification are truly necessary for everyone who becomes God's dwelling-place, just as the temple of God is holy and just as the holy place is [holy] and of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
